facts.fact: The Bank of Algeria published instruction no. 06-2025 of 17 August 2025 setting the organisation and operating rules of payment service providers, completing regulation no. 25-02 of 14 April 2025 on their authorisation and licensing (Algérie Éco, 19 August 2025).
facts.system: Instruction n° 06-2025 and Règlement n° 25-02 on payment service providers

facts.fact: The Bank of Algeria's Monetary and Banking Council communiqué of 23 September 2026 applies regulation no. 25-02 on payment service providers, a class of actors created under Monetary and Banking Law no. 23-09, in authorising a firm to constitute itself.
facts.system: Loi n° 23-09 and Règlement n° 25-02 on payment service providers

facts.fact: The Council authorised Djezzy Payment Services, a subsidiary of telecom operator Optimum Telecom Algérie, to constitute itself as a payment service provider under regulation no. 25-02; this is authorisation of constitution, with an application for licensing (agrément) due within 12 months of notification.
facts.system: Règlement n° 25-02 on payment service providers

facts.fact: Le Provincial reported on 24 September 2026 that the Bank of Algeria acted on 23 September under law no. 23-09 and regulation no. 25-02 on payment service providers, which lists services they may offer including payment accounts, transfers, card issuing, merchant acquiring and money transfer.
facts.system: Loi n° 23-09 and Règlement n° 25-02 on payment service providers

facts.fact: Le Provincial describes a payment service provider under regulation 25-02 as a new financial actor, not necessarily a bank, and reports that mobile operator subsidiary Djezzy Payment Services was authorised to constitute itself as one on 23 September 2026, with licensing (agrément) still to be applied for within 12 months.
facts.system: Règlement n° 25-02 on payment service providers

note: Banking Commission guideline 06/2025 of 12 Nov 2025 on virtual assets and AML for banks and Algerie Poste: a virtual-asset rule, class other, and it states nothing on payment-provider licensing, e-money rules or connection.

Regulation 25-14 of 24 Sept 2025 amends the AML regulation 24-03 to apply it to payment service providers; an anti-money-laundering rule (class other) that names PSPs as obliged entities but does not say they are non-banks, licensed, or required to connect.

facts.fact: The Bank of Algeria made Regulation no. 25-02 of 14 April 2025, published in Journal Officiel no. 28 of 7 May 2025, setting the conditions for authorisation, licensing and operation of payment service providers (PSPs), issued under monetary and banking law no. 23-09 of 21 June 2023.
facts.system: Regulation no. 25-02 on payment service providers

facts.fact: Regulation no. 25-02 (14 April 2025) lets a company formed under article 91 of law 23-09 be licensed as a PSP by the Governor of the Bank of Algeria after Monetary and Banking Council authorisation, with a minimum capital of DZD 160,000,000 (arts. 2, 10, 11, 14, 16), to run payment accounts, transfers, acquiring and money remittance.
facts.system: Regulation no. 25-02 on payment service providers

facts.fact: Article 19 of Regulation no. 25-02 (14 April 2025) requires a PSP's payment platform to be interoperable with every authorisation platform of the payment instruments the PSP accepts; article 6 defines interoperability as connecting the PSP platform to the issuers' authorisation platforms; it sets no deadline and names no national switch.
facts.system: Regulation no. 25-02 on payment service providers

facts.fact: Loi n° 23-09 of 21 June 2023 on money and banking, published in Journal officiel n° 43 of 27 June 2023, defines payment instruments to include electronic money (art. 74), provides for payment service providers (PSP) to be licensed under a Monetary and Banking Council regulation (art. 76), and repeals ordonnance n° 03-11 (art. 166).
facts.system: Loi n° 23-09 portant loi monétaire et bancaire

facts.fact: Loi n° 23-09 of 21 June 2023 (art. 76) lets payment services be provided by duly licensed payment service providers (PSP), with licensing terms set by Council regulation; the law lists PSPs separately from banks and financial institutions (arts. 38, 102).
facts.system: Loi n° 23-09 portant loi monétaire et bancaire
